title: Hummingbird Implementation Acceleration Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Hummingbird's Redwood deployment. Confirmed goals: staging access, SSO, network handoff, and a two-week sprint-zero to validate latency and observability. Agreed to run a small benchmark with Hummingbird sample prompts and follow-up deep dive on SSO and VPC next week.
next_steps: Jordan to share onboarding-runbook-v2 and SLA deck (by 2026-05-01)
Marcus to provide network CIDR and firewall egress list (by 2026-05-03)
Priya to schedule SSO deep-dive with Marcus and Tom (week of 2026-05-04)
Cam to set up staging tenant and invite Hummingbird team to Console (by 2026-05-02)
Tom to upload sample prompt set and a 500-request benchmark script (by 2026-05-06)
action_items: Jordan Myers: send onboarding-runbook-v2, SLA/price sheet - due 2026-05-01
Marcus Lee: share VPC CIDR, allowed egress and proxy details - due 2026-05-03
Priya Shah: prepare SSO checklist and SAML metadata example - due 2026-05-04
Cam Nguyen: provision staging tenant and add RBAC roles for Hummingbird - due 2026-05-02
Tom Rivers: deliver sample prompts + benchmark script - due 2026-05-06
questions: Elena: can we restrict logs retention to 30 days for PII minimization?
Marcus: are there additional firewall rules for KV cache used by the runtime?
Asha: what is the expected lead time for Dedicated pool vs hosted?
Tom: how granular is token-level cost breakdown in Console?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check, audio OK?
[00:06] Elena (CTO): Yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. So agenda: sprint-zero plan, networking/VPC, SSO, and what success looks like in 30 days. We'll keep this light and call out owners.
[00:28] Cam (CSM): Welcome Hummingbird team, excited to kick this off. I'll be your day-to-day contact after initial setup.
[00:36] Marcus (Lead DevOps): Appreciate it. We've got some constraints - corporate proxy, strict egress controls.
[00:44] Priya (SE): Noted. We'll need the egress CIDRs and any proxy headers. Also quick note: Redwood uses prefix/KV caching which can require a couple outbound ranges depending on runtime variant.
[01:12] Marcus: Okay, I can pull that together. Also, performance is important; we expect sub-200ms token latency for interactive flows if possible.
[01:25] Jordan: Understood. We'll baseline hosted and then recommend quantization/variant or Dedicated if the numbers justify it.
[01:35] Asha (Product): Our initial use is an assisted triage chat, about 80% short prompts, 20% long context. Cost is a concern, so guidance on batching/caching would help.
[01:51] Priya: Sounds like Optimize recommendations will be useful — we'll propose batching and prefix cache; sometimes small model variants hit sweet spot for cost/latency.
[02:05] Tom (ML Eng): Two quick asks: can we limit logs retention, and does Redwood's private (VPC) option support HSM-based keys?
[02:15] Cam: Yes to retention settings — we can set retention per workspace. For KMS/HSM, that's available on Private with enterprise package; we'll surface the doc.
[02:27] Elena: We also need SOC 2 evidence and audit logs for compliance.
[02:34] Jordan: We'll attach SOC 2 Type II, and the Console supports audit logs exports. I'll include links in the runbook.
[02:45] Marcus: On networking, we have a corporate NAT proxy that rewrites TLS. That sometimes breaks mTLS style flows.
[02:55] Priya: Hmm, we've seen proxy rewrites cause header truncation. For the staging tenant, we can test with a small VM behind the proxy; if it fails, Dedicated in VPC would be the fallback.
[03:12] Asha: Timeline-wise, we want a pilot within 3 weeks, production-ready in 8 weeks. Is that realistic?
[03:22] Jordan: Pilot in 3 weeks is doable if staging access and SSO are set up quickly. Production in 8 weeks depends on network and legal sign-offs.
[03:30] Cam: We'll prioritize staging and SSO first week, then performance validation week two.
[03:40] Tom: Regarding SSO, we use Okta and want SCIM for user provisioning.
[03:45] Priya: Okta + SAML + SCIM is in our standard flow. I'll prepare a checklist and metadata examples.
[04:00] Jordan: For the sprint-zero tasks: 1) staging tenant provision, 2) network handshake, 3) SSO config, 4) sample prompt benchmark.
[04:10] Elena: Who's doing what?
[04:14] Cam: Jordan will send the runbook and SLA/pricing. Marcus will provide network details. Priya will do the SSO deep-dive. Tom will prep prompts.
[04:30] Marcus: About telemetry: can we export latency and token-cost per request to our Prometheus?
[04:36] Priya: We have tracing hooks and a metrics export—can push to a prometheus gateway or provide a hosted dashboard. We'll map available metrics.
[04:49] Marcus: Good. If we can ingest latency histograms that's ideal.
[05:00] Asha: Any thoughts on canary deploys? We want a staged rollout to 5% then 25% then 100% and automatic rollback.
[05:08] Jordan: Redwood Console supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to a safe model variant. We'll walk through a canary plan in the ops doc.
[05:20] Tom: One more on data residency — we need EU-only for certain datasets.
[05:25] Cam: Noted. We can pin routing by region; will include guidance.
[05:34] Elena: Pricing question — we have budget constraints; how much will Dedicated cost vs hosted?
[05:42] Jordan: I'll send a model (TCO worksheet) in the runbook. As a heuristic, small Dedicated pools have higher commits but lower per-token cost at scale; we'll show a break-even.
[05:55] Marcus: For the staging tenant, we need RBAC so not everyone sees logs.
[06:02] Priya: We'll set up RBAC roles (admin, dev, auditor) in staging. Cam will provision.
[06:12] Elena: Anything else on compliance?
[06:16] Jordan: We'll get SOC 2, encryption-at-rest, and KMS options included. If you need HSM we'll open an enterprise thread.
[06:29] Asha: Can Redwood integrate with our ticketing to auto-create incidents on model degradation?
[06:34] Priya: Yes—webhooks for alerts and a webhook-connector for Jira/ServiceNow. We'll share a sample integration.
[06:45] Tom: Regarding performance tests, what's a recommended load pattern?
[06:49] Jordan: Start with a 500-request spike at expected concurrency, then steady for 10 minutes; include mixed prompt lengths. That'll surface batching behavior.
[07:01] Marcus: We'll aim to run that after staging is up.
[07:06] Jordan: Great. I'll follow up with the runbook, SLA deck, and a checklist. Priya will schedule SSO-only deep dive. Cam will provision staging and add the Hummingbird team.
[07:18] Elena: Sounds good. Also, we may evaluate InferX for edge inference later, but for now primary is Redwood.
[07:26] Jordan: Noted. We'll include migration notes if you ever go hybrid.
[07:33] Asha: Can you send a short video demo of Console features for execs?
[07:38] Cam: Yep, we have a 6-minute tour I'll attach.
[07:44] Marcus: Any blocker on our side? We need to confirm who handles firewall changes.
[07:49] Elena: I'll own the approvals; Marcus will implement.
[07:54] Jordan: Excellent. We'll reconvene after staging is provisioned. Any last questions?
[08:01] Tom: Just one — token accounting for embeddings vs generation, are they separate meters?
[08:06] Priya: Yes, Console splits embeddings and generation — token-metering is per-route. We'll show an example.
[08:16] Elena: Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Jordan: Thanks. Meeting adjourned.

Notes and links mentioned: onboarding-runbook-v2 (link attached in follow-up email), SLA and pricing spreadsheet, Console demo video, metrics export guide, SOC2 PDF.

Caveats in transcript: occasional mis-heard words; speaker labels auto-generated and may be slightly off in a few places.
